banh-dap-cam-nam-hoi-an.name: Cẩm Nam smashed rice crackers
banh-dap-cam-nam-hoi-an.serving_basis: Four portions of crisp rice crackers layered with soft steamed rice sheets and pineapple mam nem.
banh-dap-cam-nam-hoi-an.description: In Cam Nam, banh dap pairs a soft steamed rice sheet between crisp rice crackers, broken by hand and dipped in mam nem. Bep Viet has adapted the local combination for home cooking, keeping the dipping sauce separate so each person can adjust it.
banh-dap-cam-nam-hoi-an.finished_dish: Crisp rice crackers sandwich a soft rice sheet, served with pineapple, garlic and chili mam nem.
banh-dap-cam-nam-hoi-an.serving: Serve as soon as assembled so the crackers stay crisp. Keep the mam nem dip separate and serve with herbs and cucumber.
banh-dap-cam-nam-hoi-an.image_alt: Crisp Cẩm Nam rice crackers sandwich soft steamed rice sheets, served with pineapple, garlic and chili mam nem.
banh-dap-cam-nam-hoi-an.time_note: Assemble the toasted rice crackers and steamed sheets close to serving so the crackers stay crisp.
tips: Let the rice sheets cool and dry slightly before assembling so the crackers do not soften too quickly.
Toast the rice crackers over low heat, turning frequently until crisp and puffed without scorching.
Season the mam nem gradually because saltiness varies by brand.

ingredients.name: Round rice crackers
ingredients.notes: Toast until crisp shortly before serving.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Sift until fine for smooth rice sheets.

ingredients.name: Tapioca starch
ingredients.notes: Adds a gentle chew to the steamed rice sheets.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Adjust until the batter pours in a thin stream.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For brushing the pan and mixing with scallions.

ingredients.name: Red chilli
ingredients.notes: Remove the seeds for a milder heat.

preparation_steps: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, water and salt until smooth. Rest for 10 minutes, then whisk again; stir before each sheet if the batter settles.
Slice the scallions and toss them with a teaspoon of hot oil. Mince the pineapple, garlic and chili separately for the dip.
Wash and thoroughly drain the herbs and cucumber. Set out the rice crackers to toast shortly before serving.
cooking_steps: Heat a nonstick skillet and brush with a very thin film of oil. Pour in a ladle of batter, swirl into a thin sheet, cover and cook for 40–60 seconds until translucent and set. Sprinkle with scallions and repeat to make about eight rice sheets.
Toast the rice crackers over low heat or in a dry skillet, turning until crisp. Do not let them darken too much.
Stir the fermented fish sauce with pineapple, garlic, chili, sugar and lime juice. Taste, then add warm water gradually if the flavor is too intense.
Place a steamed rice sheet on a rice cracker and fold it or sandwich it with another cracker. Cut into bite-sized pieces and serve with herbs, cucumber and mam nem.

bun-mam-thit-heo-da-nang.name: Da Nang vermicelli with pork and fermented fish sauce
aliases: Da Nang vermicelli with fermented anchovy sauce
Da Nang boiled meat and fish sauce noodle soup
bun-mam-thit-heo-da-nang.serving_basis: Four bowls of dry vermicelli with roast pork, young jackfruit, fresh greens, pickled papaya and fermented fish sauce.
bun-mam-thit-heo-da-nang.description: Da Nang bun mam is a dry vermicelli dish with pork, young jackfruit, fresh greens, pickled papaya, peanuts and fermented fish sauce. Bep Viet uses ready-cooked roast pork for a quicker meal and balances the savory sauce with pineapple.
bun-mam-thit-heo-da-nang.finished_dish: A dry noodle bowl with fragrant roast pork, tender young jackfruit, crisp greens and gently spicy pineapple mam nem, finished with roasted peanuts.
bun-mam-thit-heo-da-nang.serving: Arrange the vermicelli, pork, jackfruit, pickled papaya, greens and cucumber in bowls. Add just enough mam nem, top with peanuts and toss just before eating.
bun-mam-thit-heo-da-nang.image_alt: A dry Da Nang bun mam bowl with roast pork, young jackfruit, pickled papaya, fresh greens, peanuts and fermented fish sauce.
bun-mam-thit-heo-da-nang.time_note: This quick version uses fully cooked roast pork and is served without broth.
tips: Add the mam nem a little at a time, tasting it with the noodles and greens to avoid over-seasoning.
If using boiled young jackfruit, drain it well and tear it into bite-sized pieces.
Store purchased roast pork safely in the refrigerator and reheat it thoroughly before serving.
keywords: Da Nang vermicelli with pork and fermented fish sauce
Da Nang vermicelli with fermented anchovy sauce
Da Nang boiled meat and fish sauce noodle soup

ingredients.name: Fresh rice vermicelli
ingredients.notes: Briefly blanch if the vermicelli is cold.

ingredients.name: Boiled young jackfruit
ingredients.notes: Drain and tear into bite-sized pieces.

ingredients.name: Pickled green papaya
ingredients.notes: Squeeze gently to remove excess brine.

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually to mellow the sauce.

preparation_steps: Wash and drain the greens, then cut the cucumber into strips. Tear the young jackfruit into bite-sized pieces and slice the pickled papaya and roast pork.
Mince the garlic, chili and pineapple. If needed, toast the peanuts, then crush them coarsely for garnish.
cooking_steps: Stir the fermented fish sauce with pineapple, garlic, chili and sugar. Gradually add warm water, balancing salty, sweet and sour flavors; finish with lime juice.
If the roast pork has been refrigerated, reheat it until hot throughout before slicing; do not leave it at room temperature for long.
Briefly blanch the vermicelli if needed and drain. Divide it among four bowls, arranging the pork, jackfruit, papaya, cucumber and greens around it.
Add just enough mam nem and sprinkle with roasted peanuts. Toss just before eating and serve any remaining sauce on the side.

banh-ep-thuan-an-hue.name: Thuan An pressed tapioca cakes
banh-ep-thuan-an-hue.serving_basis: Four portions of tapioca cakes filled with pork and egg, served with herbs, pickles and a mildly spicy dip.
banh-ep-thuan-an-hue.description: Thuan An pressed cakes have a thin, chewy tapioca wrapper cooked with pork, egg and scallions; they can be served soft or pressed until drier. Bep Viet has adapted the method for a home griddle or press and serves them with fresh herbs, pickles and dipping sauce.
banh-ep-thuan-an-hue.finished_dish: Hot, lightly golden tapioca cakes wrap a chewy pork-and-egg filling; fresh herbs and pickled papaya balance each bite.
banh-ep-thuan-an-hue.serving: Eat while hot, wrapped or served with fresh herbs and pickled papaya; dip in a lightly diluted chili fish sauce.
banh-ep-thuan-an-hue.image_alt: Hot, thin Thuan An tapioca cakes filled with pork, egg and scallions, served with herbs, pickled papaya and dipping sauce.
banh-ep-thuan-an-hue.time_note: The amount of water depends on the starch; add boiling water gradually and stop once the dough is pliable.
tips: Knead while the water is still hot, but let it cool enough to handle. Add it gradually until the dough is pliable, not sticky.
Press the cakes thinly and spread the filling evenly so the dough cooks through before the surface darkens.
Adjust crispness by changing the pressing time; avoid drying the cakes so much that they become hard.

ingredients.name: Boiling water
ingredients.notes: Pour gradually; the amount may vary with the flour.

ingredients.name: Ground pork shoulder
ingredients.notes: A little fat keeps the topping tender.

preparation_steps: Mix the tapioca starch with salt. Gradually stir in boiling water with a spoon; once cool enough, knead until soft and pliable without sticking. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Marinate the ground pork with shallots, fish sauce and pepper for 10 minutes. Wash and drain the greens; prepare the pickled papaya and dipping sauce.
cooking_steps: Divide the dough into 12 small balls. Roll each into a thin round about 8–10 cm wide on a lightly floured surface.

Heat a cast-iron or heavy-bottomed skillet over medium heat and brush with a little oil. Place a dough round in the pan, spread on a spoonful of pork, add a little beaten egg and sprinkle with scallions.
Cover or press flat for 1–2 minutes, flip and press again until the wrapper turns translucent and the filling is fully cooked. For a drier cake, leave it on the pan a little longer.
Transfer the cake to a plate and repeat with the remaining dough and filling. Serve hot with herbs, pickled papaya and chili fish sauce.

cha-chia-ha-lung.name: Ha Lung sugarcane squid patties
cha-chia-ha-lung.serving_basis: Four servings of squid-and-pork patties molded around sugarcane, steamed and lightly seared in Bep Viet's home adaptation.
cha-chia-ha-lung.description: Ha Lung cha chia combines pounded squid and pork molded around sugarcane, bringing savory seafood flavor and a gentle sweetness. For this small home batch, Bep Viet steams the patties to keep them moist, then lightly sears them for a golden surface.
cha-chia-ha-lung.finished_dish: Golden patties with a tender, springy squid-and-pork center, served on sugarcane sticks for a subtle sweetness.
cha-chia-ha-lung.serving: Serve hot with fresh herbs and chili fish sauce. Hold by the sugarcane stick, or remove it before serving to young children.
cha-chia-ha-lung.image_alt: Ha Lung cha chia are squid-and-pork patties molded around sugarcane, steamed and lightly browned.
cha-chia-ha-lung.time_note: Steaming cooks the pork and squid evenly; the quick sear is only for color and aroma.
tips: Use fresh, well-drained squid and pound or pulse until tacky; avoid over-processing, which can warm the mixture.
Mold a moderate layer of mixture around the sugarcane so the center cooks evenly.
Steam the patties through before searing briefly; make sure the center is fully cooked before serving.

ingredients.name: Dried wood ear mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Soak until rehydrated, rinse and mince.

ingredients.name: Sugarcane
ingredients.notes: Cut into sticks about 8 cm long and peel the handle end.

preparation_steps: Clean and thoroughly dry the squid, then chop or pulse it coarsely. Soak the shiitake and wood ear mushrooms until rehydrated, rinse, squeeze dry and mince.
Cut the sugarcane into short sticks and peel the handle ends. Mix the squid, pork, mushrooms, shallots, fish sauce, sugar and pepper; pound or mix until tacky, then chill for 15 minutes.
cooking_steps: Divide the mixture into eight portions. Wet your hands and mold each portion around one end of a sugarcane stick, leaving about 4 cm exposed as a handle.
Arrange the patties in a preheated steamer and steam for 12–15 minutes until fully cooked. Leave space between them.
Heat a little oil in a nonstick skillet and sear the steamed patties for 1–2 minutes per side until lightly golden, rolling them to brown evenly.
Serve hot with herbs and spicy-sour fish sauce. Wash and peel the sugarcane sticks thoroughly before they touch the food.

banh-gai-ninh-giang.name: Ninh Giang ramie-leaf cakes
banh-gai-ninh-giang.serving_basis: Eight ramie-leaf sticky-rice cakes filled with mung beans, coconut, sweetened pork fat and candied winter melon, wrapped in banana leaves and steamed.
banh-gai-ninh-giang.description: Ninh Giang banh gai are known for their glossy, chewy black glutinous-rice wrapper colored with ramie leaves. The filling combines mung beans, coconut, sweetened pork fat and candied winter melon, wrapped in dried banana leaves. Bep Viet has edited a small-batch method while retaining these signature ingredients and noting the soaking and steaming time.
banh-gai-ninh-giang.finished_dish: A chewy black ramie and glutinous-rice wrapper surrounds a fragrant mung-bean and coconut filling with sweetened pork fat and candied winter melon.
banh-gai-ninh-giang.serving: Let the cakes cool slightly after steaming, then unwrap the banana leaves and serve as a snack or edible gift. Keep leftovers wrapped to preserve freshness.
banh-gai-ninh-giang.image_alt: Ninh Giang banh gai with a glossy black ramie sticky-rice wrapper, mung-bean and coconut filling, and banana-leaf wrapping.
banh-gai-ninh-giang.time_note: The rice and mung beans need advance soaking; allow about 6 hours of hands-off time, not including cooling.
tips: Soak the glutinous rice long enough to hydrate evenly, then drain it thoroughly before grinding or pounding.
Boil the ramie leaves until tender, remove tough veins and pound or blend until smooth for a silky wrapper.
Steam until the wrappers are evenly chewy; timing depends on cake size and how tightly the steamer is covered.

ingredients.name: Cái Hoa Vàng glutinous rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse and soak for 6 hours or overnight.

ingredients.name: Fresh ramie leaves
ingredients.notes: Pick tender leaves and remove the stems and tough veins.

ingredients.name: Pork fat
ingredients.notes: Dice and render until the cracklings and clear fat separate.

ingredients.name: Dried banana leaves
ingredients.notes: Warm until pliable and wipe clean before wrapping.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Brush lightly onto the wrapper if needed.

preparation_steps: Rinse the glutinous rice until the water runs clear and soak for 6 hours or overnight. Soak the mung beans separately for about 2 hours, then drain both well.
Wash and boil the ramie leaves until tender. Remove tough veins and pound or blend until very smooth, adding a little cooking water if needed.
Steam the mung beans until soft and mash them. Render the pork fat; mix the beans with sugar, coconut, candied winter melon, some rendered fat and sesame for the filling.
cooking_steps: Grind or pound the soaked rice into a sticky dough. Mix with the ramie paste, remaining sugar and a little salt; knead until evenly dark, then divide into eight portions.
Shape the filling into eight balls. Enclose each with a portion of the ramie-rice dough, sealing the seam so the filling stays inside while steaming.
Warm the dried banana leaves until pliable, wipe clean and cut to size. Place each cake in the center, wrap into a small packet and set it seam-side down.

Bring water to a boil in a steamer. Steam the cakes for 75–90 minutes depending on size, maintaining a steady boil and adding hot water if needed. Rest in the steamer for 10 minutes, then remove and cool.
